_note: Sitting Maine, Colorado, Minnesota and Nevada state legislators, read on 2026-10-28 from the Open States current-legislator lists (compiled from each Legislature's own member pages) and checked against the Colorado General Assembly's member list and the Minnesota House's member list. cmp-data.js carries a roster shell for every "rows" entry; "alreadyHeld" are existing records that already named the seat; "districtSet" names existing leadership records that gained their district; "seatedFromCandidacy" names sitting members who were on the roster only as a 2026 federal or statewide candidacy — their row now names the seat they hold and the candidacy moved to window.CMP_CANDIDACIES. scripts/gen-district-boards.mjs opens a read-only board for every seat (a contested Colorado or Minnesota seat keeps the voice it had). Every chamber is full: Colorado House District 32 is held by Maria Gonzalez, appointed after Manny Rutinel resigned on 2026-09-04, and Minnesota House District 21A by Joe Schomacker; both are on their chamber's own list and not yet on Open States', and their rows cite the chamber list. Maine's two tribal representatives (Passamaquoddy Tribe and Houlton Band of Maliseet Indians) are non-voting, hold no district and have no row. Three Maine senators already carried an id in state-senate-stances-w13.js (mattie_daughtry, teresa_pierce, trey_stewart); their shells use it. Four display names are shared with an unrelated record in another state: Colorado Rep. Dusty Johnson (johnson_co) is not South Dakota's U.S. Rep. Dusty Johnson; Maine Rep. Chad Perkins (perkins_me) is not Missouri's (perkins_mo); Minnesota Rep. Ben Davis (davis_mn) is not Montana's House candidate (ben_davis); Minnesota Sen. Bill Weber (weber_mn) is not New York's (weber_ny).
